subject: AtlasAI perf/discovery — context ceiling & streaming hedges
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Marissa —

Thanks again for the call earlier. A couple of clarifying points from our side so engineering can size the POC:

- Primary flow: ingest ~6–8KB of structured JSON (metadata + 1–3 long fields) per request, then generate a summarized extraction + 2 candidate suggested actions (~350–700 tokens out).
- Peak concurrency expected during business hours: ~35–45 concurrent user requests (mostly short bursts).
- SLO goals: p95 end-to-end server-side latency <= 300 ms for 512 tokens output; soft p99 target <= 700 ms.
- Streaming: we want server-sent events for the suggestion stream; client wants first token within 120 ms ideally.
- Context window: some requests will include a rolling patient note history up to ~8k tokens; worst-case combined input+output could approach 10–11k tokens.

I've attached a small latency sample and a couple hundred example requests. Can you confirm whether Redwood has recommended model variants and routing policy for this profile, and whether there are straightforward hedges if we hit token-ceiling latencies?

Next steps from AtlasAI:
- We can start a week-long perf sweep if Redwood shares recommended perf config (batching, quantization, concurrency limits).
- Need an estimate for incremental cost if we enable dedicated capacity with a 99ms p95 target vs 300ms p95.

Thanks —
Alex
Sr. Eng Manager, Integrations
AtlasAI


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Alex — great notes, thanks for laying that out. Looping in Connor (serving/runtime lead) to provide the perf checklist and an initial hedging plan.

High-level responses now, Connor will expand:
- Model variants: for 10–11k combined token windows we recommend testing a 13B quantized variant (NVQ8 or FP16 depending on accuracy needs) and a 30B lightly quantized model as a fallback for latency-sensitive flows.
- Streaming: Redwood supports early token flush (streaming chunk size tunable). First-byte latency depends on batching and concurrency — see Connor's matrix below.
- Token ceiling hedges: automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated history and a deterministic truncation + summarize-before-run path we usually propose.

Action items for this week:
1) Connor: perf matrix + recommended batch settings and expected p95 ranges for each model variant.
2) Alex: share a representative 24-hour envelope (traffic distribution) and mark % of requests that include the full 8k note history.
3) Marissa/AtlasAI: agree schedule for 5-day perf sweep (we recommend starting with dev dedicated pool).

I'll follow up with an annotated example config.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Alex — quick technical breakdown (summary first, followed by numbers):

Summary:
- Baseline: for the ingest + 512–700 token output profile with 8k input, expect p95 latency in the 350–600 ms range on a high-throughput shared-hosted config (NVidia A100 class), depending on batching and KV cache hits.
- For p95 <= 300 ms we recommend dedicated capacity sized to keep effective batch sizes small (1–4 tokens per request at the decoding stage) and prefer FP16 kernels; that typically requires 1–2 reserved GPU-enabled workers per ~40 rps sustained for this model size.
- For first-byte streaming <= 120 ms: tune streaming_chunk_ms to 50–100ms and set max_batch_latency to 30–50ms (lower batch latency increases per-token cost).

Numbers / configuration guidance:
- Recommended models to run initial sweep: 13B-quant (nvq8) and 30B-fp16 fallback.
- Concurrency assumptions and expected p95 (approx):
  * 20 concurrent rps (low): 13B-quant p95 ~220–300 ms for 512-token output (8k input, KV miss).
  * 40 concurrent rps (target): 13B-quant p95 ~350–520 ms (depends heavily on batching).
  * 80 concurrent rps (burst): expect p95 to shift to 600–1,200 ms unless autoscaling/dedicated capacity is provisioned.
- Throughput: token/s served per GPU (13B-quant) under steady streaming decode ~12k–18k tokens/s depending on sequence length and kernel choice.

Hedge options (when approaching token ceiling latency):
1) Summarize-before-run: pre-run cheap summarization to reduce input to <2k tokens. Good for accuracy-preserving use cases.
2) Prefix KV caching: cache embeddings/kv for repeated patient history — hits drop compute dramatically.
3) Deterministic truncation + metadata-only heuristic: drop older low-signal segments and rely on retrieval of key events.
4) Fallback routing: if p95 crosses threshold, route to smaller FP16 model with a slightly lower quality but better latency.

Estimator for cost delta (very rough):
- Hosted shared: baseline cost index = 1.0 (13B-quant).
- Dedicated to hit p95 99 ms: ~3x cost multiplier due to reserved GPUs and smaller batching.

Suggested next steps:
- AtlasAI provides the 24-hr envelope and sample traffic (Alex).
- Redwood will provision a 5-day dev dedicated pool and populate with both model variants; we'll run a ramped stress sweep and share p50/p95/p99 with the sample set.

I'll attach a small perf matrix CSV and an example jsonl of telemetry we need (attached).

Connor O'Brien
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Thanks Marissa/Connor — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifications after reviewing Connor's notes:

- Percentage of full-history requests: ~18% of traffic includes the full ~8k note history; most are <1.5k tokens. We'll flag the examples in the sample set.
- For summarization-before-run: AtlasAI prefers an on-path heuristic (lightweight local summarizer) vs an upstream offline job — any pointers on latency budget for that extra step?
- Cost: AtlasAI will evaluate the 3x multiplier vs product impact. Can Redwood share rough runbook for canarying the fallback routing so we can validate no regressions in suggestion quality?

We've uploaded the 24hr envelope and sample requests to the Drive link (same folder as the attachments). Let's schedule the perf sweep to start next Tuesday (2027-05-04) if that works for the Redwood team.

Next steps agreed:
- AtlasAI: confirm start date and mark examples with the full-history indicator (by EOD 2027-04-28).
- Redwood: send the dev-dedicated pool sizing and day-1 config by 2027-04-29.
- Both: set up a 30-minute kickoff on 2027-05-04 to align on runbook and success metrics.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Alex
Sr. Eng Manager, Integrations
AtlasAI
